skill.name: routeros-app-yaml
skill.description: Helps write and review RouterOS /app YAML for MikroTik container applications. Covers service fields, ports, placeholders, app stores, REST usage, and validation schemas.
skill.summary: Create and validate RouterOS /app YAML for MikroTik container applications.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: All static command, network, role-token, and reconnaissance detections were reviewed as false positives in documentation or YAML examples. No prompt injection, host command execution, or unauthorized network behavior was found. Two content risks remain: weak example credentials and mutable image update patterns.

remediation.issue: Deployable examples use weak default credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Replace admin:admin, changeme, and admin with placeholder secret names and warn users to set unique credentials.

remediation.issue: Examples use mutable latest image tags with auto-update behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer pinned image versions or digests in examples, especially when auto-update is enabled.

remediation.issue: The /bin/sh entrypoint example can encourage broad shell invocation.
remediation.suggestion: Use direct container commands where possible, or state why shell entrypoints are needed.

static_findings.snippet: RouterOS 7.21 introduced the `/app` path (built-in app listing and management). The full YAML app cr
The `/app` subsystem lets users define one or more containers as a single "application" in YAML. Rou
- Each `/app` is defined by a YAML document with services, configs, volumes, and networks
- The YAML is loaded into RouterOS via CLI (`/app/add yaml-url=...`) or REST API
- Built-in apps ship with RouterOS (visible at `GET /rest/app`)
| Environment | `KEY=value` or list | Same, but placeholders expand |
| Configs | Docker configs API | Inline `content` only |
| `name` | string | No | Unique identifier for the /app |
| `descr` | string | No | Human-readable description shown in app UI |
| `icon` | string (URI) | No | Icon URL (shown in WebFig with `show-in-webfig=yes`) |
| `default-credentials` | string or null | No | `username:password` shown in UI |
| `url-path` | string | No | URL path suffix for browser access (e.g., `/admin`) |
| `credentials` | string | No | Credential hint (alternative to default-credentials) |
| `option` | boolean | No | Whether app is optional |
| `auto-update` | boolean | No | Pull and restart containers on every boot |
| `configs` | object | No | Config file declarations with inline content |
Each key under `services:` defines one container. Required property: `image`.
| `image` | string | Container image (omit registry to use `/container/config`'s `registry-url`) |
| `container_name` | string | Explicit name; used as base for file paths under `/container` |
| `entrypoint` | string or string[] | Override default entrypoint |
| `command` | string or string[] | Override default command |
| `environment` | object or array or null | Environment variables (`KEY=value` list or `{KEY: value}
| `configs` | array of objects | Config file placements (`{source, target, mode}`) |
| `depends_on` | array or object | Service dependency ordering |
| `devices` | array of strings | Device mappings passed to container |
| `user` | string | User to run container as |
| `stop_grace_period` | string or int | Time before SIGKILL |
| `build` | object or string | Build configuration (context, dockerfile, args) |
| `healthcheck` | object | Health check (test, interval, timeout, retries, start_period) |
| `expose` | array | Internal ports (not published to host) |
| `secrets` | array of strings | Secrets to expose |
| `[accessIP]` | IP address for accessing the app from outside |
| `[accessPort]` | Primary host port for external access |
| `[containerIP]` | IP address assigned to the container |

Store files use the `.tikappstore.yaml` extension by convention.

**Note:** The `/app` endpoint requires the **container** extra package to be installed.
| `*.latest.json` | CI/strict validation | Regex patterns enforced | `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$` only |
| `*.editor.json` | Editor/SchemaStore UX | No regex (allows autocompletion) | Case-insensitive |
The strict schema has regex `pattern` on port strings which **prevents VSCode autocompletion** — the
Use `.editor.json` URLs for better autocompletion at the cost of less strict validation.
- **Using `version:` key** — RouterOS ignores it; not needed
- **Uppercase env var names required** in strict validation — use `*.editor.json` for mixed case
- **Forgetting the container package** — `/app` returns 404 without the `container` extra package
- For RouterOS fundamentals, CLI syntax, REST API: see the `routeros-fundamentals` skill

semantic_findings.title: Weak Default Credentials in Examples
semantic_findings.description: Deployable YAML examples include default or placeholder credentials such as admin:admin, changeme, and admin. Users may copy these values into production manifests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential values are present in deployable examples and are commonly copied. They are likely instructional placeholders, so the risk is content guidance rather than malicious behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Container Images with Auto Update
semantic_findings.description: Examples combine auto-update behavior with mutable latest image tags. This can pull unreviewed container changes if users copy the examples into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines show auto-update and mutable latest tags in example manifests. This is a real supply-chain risk when copied, but it is documentation rather than active code.

content.value_statement: RouterOS /app YAML differs from docker-compose and changes across RouterOS releases. This skill explains the format, validation choices, REST loading patterns, and common mistakes.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS /app top-level and service fields.
Shows old and new RouterOS port mapping formats.
Describes accessIP, accessPort, containerIP, and routerIP placeholders.
Covers app store YAML arrays and file extension conventions.
Documents REST API add and list patterns for /app.
Provides schema and VSCode YAML integration references.
limitations: Does not connect to routers or deploy apps by itself.
Does not guarantee behavior on unreleased RouterOS builds.
Needs user-provided YAML to inspect a specific manifest.
Does not replace RouterOS security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Create RouterOS App Manifests
use_cases.description: Draft valid /app YAML with services, ports, volumes, configs, and placeholders.

use_cases.title: Translate Compose Designs
use_cases.description: Map docker-compose concepts to RouterOS /app fields and identify unsupported options.

use_cases.title: Document App Store Entries
use_cases.description: Prepare app store YAML guidance, schema notes, and validation advice for router users.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Minimal App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal RouterOS /app YAML for an Nginx web service on port 8080. Explain each field briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Compose Concepts
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this docker-compose service plan into RouterOS /app YAML. Identify unsupported fields and suggest RouterOS alternatives: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this RouterOS /app YAML for port format, placeholders, environment variables, and unsupported compose keys: [paste YAML].

prompt_templates.title: Design Store Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RouterOS /app store entry for a multi-service monitoring app. Include configs, volumes, networks, validation notes, and safe credential placeholders.

output_examples.input: User asks for a minimal Nginx RouterOS app.
output_examples.output: A concise manifest outline with service name, image choice, port mapping guidance, and RouterOS version notes.

output_examples.input: User pastes a docker-compose service plan.
output: Unsupported compose fields are listed with RouterOS alternatives.
Port mappings are converted to RouterOS-supported formats.
Placeholders and validation schema choices are explained.

output_examples.input: User asks why RouterOS /app validation fails.
output_examples.output: An issue list covering port syntax, uppercase environment names, missing packages, schema choice, and version-specific support.

best_practices: Use pinned image versions or digests for production app definitions.
Replace example credentials with unique secrets before deployment.
Validate strict schemas in CI and editor schemas during authoring.
anti_patterns: Assuming docker-compose fields work unchanged in RouterOS /app.
Publishing manifests with admin:admin or changeme credentials.
Mixing old and new port mapping styles in one service.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy apps to my router?
faq.answer: No. It explains and reviews RouterOS /app YAML, but it does not connect to RouterOS devices.

faq.question: Which RouterOS versions are covered?
faq.answer: It focuses on /app listing in 7.21 and custom YAML creation in 7.22 and later.

faq.question: Is RouterOS /app the same as docker-compose?
faq.answer: No. It uses similar ideas, but many compose fields are unsupported or behave differently.

faq.question: Can it help with port mapping errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents old OCI-style mappings, newer RouterOS mappings, labels, protocols, and placeholders.

faq.question: Does it include validation schema guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains strict schema use for CI and editor schema use for autocompletion.

faq.question: Can it review app store YAML?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers app store arrays, file naming conventions, and common store entry fields.
